* * *
 JUDGMENT Parents of the deceased Sibbala Ganesh filed petition under Section 166 of IMV Act claiming compensation from the respondents who are the owner and insurer of the Car bearing No.KA-05-NC-1907 alleging that on 14.08.2022 at 10.15 p.m. when Sibbala Ganesh was traveling by sitting on the pillion of the motorcycle bearing No.AP-39-LW-3310 rode by Kiran Kumar at Madanapalle- Kadire road, near Joyes Hotel, Madanapalle town, the driver of the Car bearing No.KA-05-NC-1907 drove the same negligently, dashed the same to the motorcycle, thereby caused accident, caused grievous injuries to Ganesh.

Immediately after the accident Ganesh has been admitted to Government Hospital, Madanapalle wherein first aid has been provided, then admitted to Ramadevi Hospital, Tirupathi wherein Ganesh succumbed to the injuries on 19.08.2022.
2. Regarding accident Madanapalle Town police registered a case in crime No.150/2022 .

3. As on the date of accident Sibbala Ganesh being aged about 24 years, used to earn Rs.20,000/p.m. by working in a Private firm and used to contribute the entire income to the family.
4.

In response to the notice respondent No.1 - insurance company appeared through his Advocate filed written statement denying the allegation regarding reason, mode of the accident , age,
occupation, income of deceased Sibbala Ganesh.

5. In response to the notice respondent No.2- owner of the car appeared through his Advocate filed written statement denying the allegation regarding reason, mode of the accident , age, occupation,
income of deceased Sibbala Ganesh.
Respondent No.2 asserted that Kiran Kumar and Ganesh are riders of the motorcycle rode the same under intoxication, dashed the same to the car.

6. On the basis of the pleadings on 27.06.2023, this Authority has framed the following issues:
1. Whether the petitioners prove that, on 14.08.2022 at about 10.15 p.m. near Joyas Hotel, Madanapalle town, on Madanapalli- Kadire Road, Annamayya, Andrapradesh, the death caused to one Sibbala Ganesh was deu to actionable negligence act on the part of the driver of the Car bearing Reg. No.KA-05-NC- 1907 as Sibbala Venkataramana vs Bharathi Axa Gen Ins Co Ltd on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68352876/
2 alleged?
2.

sentences.text: Whether the petitioners are entitled to compensation ?
If so, how much and from whom?
3. What order?
7. On 14.08.2023, 13.12.2023 petitioner No.1 Sibbala Venkataramana deposed as PW1 and produced 17 documents at Ex.P.1 to P.14 and Ex.P.2(a), P.5(a), P.7(a).
8. I heard the arguments submitted on behalf of both the parties and perused the records.

9. On the basis of material available in the file, my findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1 .... In the Affirmative. Issue No.2...

Petitioners are entitle to Rs.26,32,000/-
with interest at 6%p.a. as compensation Issue No.3 ...

As per final order for the following:-
REASONS 10. Issues No.1 :- In the evidence affidavit PW1 Sibbala Venkataramana stated that on 14.08.2022 at 10.15 p.m. when Sibbala Ganesh was travelling by sitting on the pillion of the motorcycle bearing No.AP-39-LW-3310 rode by Kiran Kumar at Madanapalle- Kadire road, near Joyes Hotel,
Madanapalle town, the driver of the Car bearing No.KA-05-NC-1907 drove the same negligently,
dashed the same to the motorcycle, thereby caused accident, caused grievous injuries to Ganesh.

PW.1 further stated that immediately after the accident Ganesh has been admitted to Government Hospital, Madanapalle wherein first aid has been provided then shifted to Ramadevi Hospital,
Tirupathi wherein Ganesh succumbed to the injuries on 19.08.2022.
11.

In the written statements respondent No.1 and 2 denied the allegation regarding reason and mode of accident and asserted that due to the sole negligent riding of the motorcycle accident has taken place.
12. In the cross-examination, PW1 submitted that he have not seen the accident spot and received information from the hospital about mode of the accident.
PW.1 stated that the persons who have seen the accident and his relatives have informed him about the details of the accident.
PW.1 stated that Kiran Kumar was admitted to Government Hospital, Madaanapalli who is not in contact.
PW.1 stated that his son has been treated for 4 days in Ramadevi Hospital, Tirupati after the accident.

13. Ex.P.1 is the copy of FIR pertaining to crime No.150/2022 registered by Madanapalle Town police against Suman driver of Car bearing No.KA-05-NC-1907 for having committed offence punishable under Section 337 of IPC on the basis of the complaint presented by Madi Kiran Kumar.

Ex.P.2 and P.2(a) are the copy of complaint and English translation of complaint dated 15.08.2022 Sibbala Venkataramana vs Bharathi Axa Gen Ins Co Ltd on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68352876/
3 filed by Kiran Kumar.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Ex.P.3 is the copy of Alteration Memo dated 19.08.2022 forwarded by Station House Officer, Madanapalle Town Police Station, Chittoor to Additional Judicial Magistrate 1st Class 2.
Ex . P.5
and Ex.P.5(a) are inquest report and English translation copy of the inquest report.
Ex.P.6 is the copy of motor vehicle accident report.
Ex. P.7
and P.7(a)
are the sketch of place of accident and English translation copy sketch of place of accident.

Ex.P.8 is the copy of the charge sheet filed by Madanapalle police in crime No.150/2022 against respondent No.2 - T.M. Suman- the driver of Car bearing No.KA-05-NC-1907 for having committed offence punishable under Section 304(A) and 337 of IPC and Sec.134(A&B) r/w 187 MV Act .
In the police records name of Sibbala Ganesh is noted as pillion rider of the motorcycle and victim of the accident.
14. In this case, respondent No.1 and 2 have not produced any type of evidence to disbelieve or rebut the evidence placed by the petitioners.

Hence, I have concluded that on 14.08.2022 at 10.15 p.m.
when Sibbala Ganesh was travelling by sitting on the pillion of the motorcycle bearing No.AP-39-LW-3310 rode by Kiran Kumar at Madanapalle- Kadire road, near Joyes Hotel,
Madanapalle town, respondent No.2- Suman the driver of the Car bearing No.KA-05-NC-1907 drove the same negligently, dashed the same to the motorcycle, thereby caused accident, caused grievous injuries to Ganesh who succumbed to those injuries on 19.08.2022.
Hence, I answer issues No.1 in the affirmative.

15. Issue No.2: In the evidence affidavit PW1 has stated that as on the date of accident Sibbala Ganesh being aged about 24 years, used to earn Rs.20,000/p.m. by working in a Private firm i.e.,
Excel Private Limtied, and used to contribute entire income to the family.
16. In the written statements respondents No.1 and 2 denied the allegation regarding occupation and income of deceased Sibbala Ganesh as on the date of accident.
17. In the cross-examination PW1 stated that his son was a M.A. Graduate, there is an identity card of his son who was working in Excel Private Limited, Bengaluru .
PW.1 stated that the company has not issued any appointment letter to his son, who had account in Axis Bank.
PW.1 stated that salary was paid to his son through cash.
PW.1 submitted ignorance about the date on which day his son joined for the job.
PW.1 admitted that the lack of documents to show that his son was getting salary worth Rs.20,000/- per month.
18. In the copy of Driving Licence at Ex.P.14 of deceased Ganesh his date of birth is noted as 04.09.1998.
The ration card and aadhaar cards shows that petitioners are the parents of Sibbala Ganesh.
19. In the file there are no documents regarding occupation and income of Sibbala Ganesh.

Hence, I have calculated the loss of dependency in the following terms:
Age of the deceased Sibbala Ganesh as on 24 years the date of accident - Monthly notional income of deceased Sibbala Rs.15,500/- Ganesh as on the date of accident Add: 50% towards future prospects Rs. 23,250/- (15,500 + 7,750= 23,250)
Sibbala Venkataramana vs Bharathi Axa Gen Ins Co Ltd on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68352876/
4

sentences.text: Less : 50% towards personal expenses of the Rs. 11,625/- deceased Sibbala Ganesh (23,250 - 11,625/- = 11,625)

Annual income of the deceased Rs.1,39,500/- Loss of dependency Rs.1,39,500x18 Rs.25,11,000/-
20.
Hence, I award Rs.25,11,000/- towards loss of dependency.

Rs.16,500/- towards loss of estate,
Rs.16,500/- towards funeral expenses, Rs.88,000/- towards filial consortium to petitioners No.1 and 2 (44,000 x 2).
21. Therefore, the total compensation awarded to petitioners is at Rs.26,32,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a..
Sl.No. Head of Compensation Amount/Rs 1. Loss of dependency 25,11,000-00 2. Loss of estate 16,500-00 3.
Funeral expenses 16,500-00 4. Loss of Consortium to 88,000-00 Rs.44,000/each Total 26,32,000-00 22.
In the written statement respondent No.2 asserted that as on the date of accident Car bearing No.KA-05-NC- 1907 had insurance coverage with respondent No.1.
In the first part of the written statement the respondent No.1 denied the issuance of policy with respect to Car bearing No.KA-05-NC-1907.
However, in the 2nd part of the written statement sought permission to defend under Sec.170 of MV Act as if insurer of the car.

Hence, I came to the conclusion that the respondents being the owner and insurer of the Car bearing No.KA-05-NC-1907 are liable to pay compensation to the petitioners and to that effect an award is to be passed .

Hence, I answer issue No.2 partly in the affirmative and pass the following :
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of IMV Act is hereby partly allowed.
The respondents shall either jointly or severally pay Rs.26,32,000/- with current and future interest at the rate of 6% p.a., to the petitioners towards compensation.
The respondents No.1 being the insurer of the Car bearing No.KA-05-NC-1907 shall deposit compensation amount within 3 months from today.
The compensation amount and interest are distributed among petitioners equally.
After deposit of the compensation amount 70%of compensation amount and interest may be released to petitioners by crediting the same to their respective bank accounts directly.

Surplus compensation amount with interest shall be deposited in any bank in the names of petitioners for a period of 3 years without permitting to create any Sibbala Venkataramana vs Bharathi Axa Gen Ins Co Ltd on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68352876/
5 encumbrances.
